blocks.text: Transition metal complexes have particular shapes, which depend on the metal's electronic configuration, the coordination number and the nature of the ligands.

items: Linear: two ligands on opposite sides of the metal ion at 180 degrees, e.g. [Ag(NH3)2]Cl and K[Ag(CN)2].

Square planar: the metal ion and four ligands lie in one plane, at the corners of a square, with 90 degree angles. This is typical of d8 ions such as Ni2+ and Pt2+ with ligands like NH3 and CN-, e.g. [Ni(CN)4]2- and [Pt(NH3)4]2+.
Tetrahedral: four ligands at the corners of a tetrahedron with 109.5 degree angles, e.g. [CoCl4]2- and [MnCl4]2-.

Octahedral: six ligands along the x, y and z axes; four form a square plane at 90 degrees and two lie above and below it, at 180 degrees to each other. This is the most common shape, e.g. [Cr(NH3)6]3+ and [Co(en)3]3+.

blocks.alt: Four ball-and-stick models, each with a red metal ion and blue ligands on green bonds: Linear (2), two ligands on opposite sides; Square Planar (4), four ligands in one plane; Tetrahedral (4); Octahedral (6).
